chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Dharih said:

I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) in the Sanctuary (Mecca) before entering it or after entering it. He said: 'It does not harm you whichever you do. And if you bathe in Mecca, there is no objection; and if you bathe in your house when you stay in Mecca, there is no objection.'

key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: Ritual bath (full body washing for purification)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform ritual bath (ghusl) in Mecca before or after entering the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in the timing and location of the ritual bath (ghusl) for pilgrims entering Mecca, affirming that whether performed before or after crossing the boundary, or within the city or at one's residence, the act remains valid. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual purity, ensuring that the sanctity of the Haram is not compromised by rigid procedural constraints regarding the physical location of the bath.
